text:
jess-support: FYI forwarded from AcmeCorp — they got charged a large prorated daily line on Azure Marketplace for 2025-11-06, ~$320, while our usage dashboard shows no corresponding spike. Can finance confirm invoice line items?

michael-finance: I see the invoice PDF. There's a "prorated daily charge" line under meterId AZ-MET-9876 for subscription sub_az_acme. Looks like quantity 12,000 and unit price $0.026 — math gives ~312. But our billing exports show ~1,200 tokens for that day.

andrew-sre: tagging for metering: can we get the raw marketplace line-item JSON from Azure for that invoice? need timestamp window and dimension name. Also can you share the account subscription id and the marketplace publisher id?

jess-support: attaching snippet from customer (redacted):
```
Invoice line: 2025-11-06T00:00:00Z | AZ-MET-9876 | Prorated daily charge | Dimension: inference-requests | Quantity: 12000 | USD: 312.00
Customer dashboard: 2025-11-06 | tokens: 1,233 | requests: 5 | hosted_model: redwood-base-1
```

hannah-ops: odd — dimension says "inference-requests" but quantity magnitude looks like it was counted in token-units. Could be a unit mismatch (tokens vs requests).

raj-sales: AcmeCorp is reporting this publicly to their finance team, need ETA on root cause.

michael-finance: looking at our marketplace metering file (metering_export_2025-11-07.csv) — there's an additional aggregation row for that subscription with dimension "token.us" with quantity 12000. So Azure invoice picked token.us but UI mapping shows requests. I'm wondering if the publisher reported two dimensions and Azure consolidated incorrectly.

andrew-sre: can someone run this query against our metering events to show raw events for sub_az_acme on 2025-11-06?
```sql
SELECT event_time, meter_dimension, reported_quantity, client_request_id
FROM marketplace_metering_events
WHERE subscription_id = 'sub_az_acme'
  AND event_time BETWEEN '2025-11-06T00:00:00Z' AND '2025-11-06T23:59:59Z'
ORDER BY event_time;
```

jess-support: ran the query (redacted IDs) — results:
```
2025-11-06T03:12:01Z | token.us | 8000 | req_abc123
2025-11-06T08:45:22Z | token.us | 4000 | req_def456
```
No "inference-requests" events present.

hannah-ops: that explains it — Azure billed token.us totals. Why does our dashboard show only 1,233 tokens? Maybe our dashboard aggregates tokens per model differently (we dedupe cached prefix tokens). Marketplace metering likely reported raw emitted tokens before our prefix-cache deduction.

andrew-sre: good theory. Two action items: 1) correlate client_request_id -> request logs to see whether token counts are raw or post-cache. 2) confirm publisher metering client used the correct unit (we should only send "inference-requests" or a normalized token unit named by us).

michael-finance: for AcmeCorp invoice remediation, we can propose a one-time credit if mismatch confirmed. Need exact numbers and proof.

raj-sales: pls keep me updated — I need a short blurb for the account team and the exec sponsor.

jess-support: I'll ask the customer for the Azure invoice PDF and permission to share our correlation logs. Also asking for the subscription GUID.

billing-bot: Created support-ticket #BILL-2025-4337 for AcmeCorp invoice dispute. SLA: 72h.

andrew-sre: I correlated client_request_id req_abc123 -> internal request id int_777 and checked kv-cache hits. For req_abc123 we emitted 8000 tokens raw, but our billing dashboard shows 650 tokens because we credited 92% of tokens to cache hits across internal stages. Marketplace metering used our published metering_client which erroneously reported the raw emitted tokens (pre-cache) in that version (v1.3.0). We have a fix in v1.3.1 to report post-cache billable tokens.

hannah-ops: timeline: deploy fix to metering client tomorrow morning, re-ingest marketplace metering for impacted invoices (manual step), and prepare credit memo calculation.

michael-finance: estimate for AcmeCorp: invoice shows 12,000 token.us => charged $312. Our dashboard billable tokens ~650 => owed credit = 12,000 - 650 = 11,350 units -> $295.10. Approve one-time credit?

raj-sales: approve. we should make this customer-facing note succinct: cause, fix, remediation.

jess-support: drafting reply to customer: short explanation + credit offer + ask for invoice PDF. Will route to finance for credit issuance once we have signed permission.

michael-finance: filing internal postmortem. Please add any timeline notes to INCIDENT-2025-11-06-METERING in postmortems channel.

andrew-sre: also note: check timezone alignment — marketplace events are in UTC; our dashboard is in account local tz which can hide rollups. Will include that in root cause.

jess-support: customer replied with PDF and subscription GUID. Share with finance privately. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
